summary: Adds one bounded opening thesis paragraph and permits direct-section glossary definitions to move into the existing appendix.

evidence.sourceGrammar: A direct section child may contain one attribute-free lead container whose sole block is its first Markdown paragraph. Appendix glossary placement is accepted only at the document root or as a direct section child; list, quote, lead and unrelated directive nesting remain invalid with authored-range diagnostics.
evidence.executionCapabilities: Trusted HAST enhancement collapses the validated lead wrapper into one semantic paragraph. Already enhanced and review-targeted glossary definitions are removed from their source section and appended in authored document order to the existing single glossary appendix.
evidence.confinement: Both transformations consume only validated MDAST/HAST already loaded from the confined source. They read no additional path, file, URL, environment value or generated artifact.
evidence.offlineBehavior: Lead presentation is static package CSS. Existing term controls and full-definition fragment links retain the package-owned offline glossary runtime in both output formats.
evidence.deterministicSerialization: One lead is first and unique per section. Root and direct-section appendix definitions retain authored document order, collision-resolved glossary IDs, review targets and identical fragment destinations without leaving source-flow placeholders.
evidence.cspAndRuntime: The feature adds no author HTML, script, style input, handler, listener, observer, storage, form, iframe, fetch, CSP source or browser synchronization branch.
evidence.accessibility: Lead remains one reviewable prose paragraph with inline Markdown semantics and restrained visual emphasis instead of an aside/callout. Moved definitions remain visible in the labelled appendix and existing keyboard-accessible term controls link to them.
evidence.byteAndPerformanceBudgets: Validation scans direct section children and enhancement flattens one bounded paragraph. Appendix movement uses the existing linear extraction traversal and adds no reader-time work.
evidence.packageDependenciesAndLicenses: No dependency or license is added. The implementation composes the typed registry, source-mapped directive validation, existing review projection, glossary ID allocator/extractor, navigation exclusion and shared CSS tokens.
evidence.compatibility: Sources without lead retain their current output. Root and inline glossary forms, prose/code term controls, review revisions, navigation, both publishers, CSP and package runtime remain compatible; the additions stay within source contract major 1.
